unknowns.question: Will Task 2 wearable persistence write into results:{id}? If so, history reads pay for wearable docs
unknowns.approach: Decide in Task 2 shaping; prefer a separate partition

knowns.fact: Must keep each biomarker's latest value and unit visible, show its history in date order with values the member can inspect, show reference ranges, use the signed-in member's results, and not rely on a table alone
Tests for the history behaviour and a short note of assumptions (NOTES.md) are required. No new ingest code
Each result keeps its as-at-draw ranges and status, and biomarkers can be missing from some draws
Store API frozen, /api/home <=35 ms p95, app/auth.py unchanged, ~20 min budget for Task 1
Add GET /api/biomarkers/{id}/history; leave /api/home alone. At 50 draws, inline history puts home p95 at 55 ms (over 35); the per-biomarker endpoint is 10.5 ms and home stays at 3.5 ms
knowns.answers: Extend GET /api/home or add a per-biomarker history endpoint, within the 35 ms p95 budget (incl. after wearable import)?

knowns.fact: Ranges drift across draws for 6/30 biomarkers; plot each point against its own as-at-draw bands (stepped), tooltip shows that draw's optimal range
knowns.answers: Plot each point against its own as-at-draw range, or a single current band?

knowns.fact: Seed data is clean (>=2 points each, no nulls/one-sided ranges) but common real-world edge cases are guarded cheaply: unknown id 404, empty 200, single point, gaps, same-date draws, missing bands, unit changes, outliers, member scoping
Inline expand under each marker card via an aria-expanded toggle (perf.js pattern); lazy fetch; Chart.js line on a linear time axis with a stepped-band plugin
knowns.answers: Which layout and interaction: inline sparkline that expands, a modal, or a detail view?

knowns.fact: Slices: 1) API endpoint + pytest; 2) inline chart with tooltips + empty state; 3) NOTES.md; extras after
knowns.answers: What's the thinnest end-to-end slice that meets every Task 1 requirement in ~20 min?

decisions.decision: Per-biomarker history endpoint (GET /api/biomarkers/{id}/history), /api/home unchanged — inlining history goes over the home budget at ~35+ draws; the endpoint pattern carries over to Task 2
Chart plots each point against its as-at-draw ranges as stepped bands, not the catalogue's current ranges
Guard common edge cases with one cheap check each, tested and listed in NOTES.md; no attempt at an infallible system
Inline expandable chart under each marker card, not a modal or detail route
Flat route module (app/routes/history.py) with a pure history_points function; no domain/service layer — one filter over one partition doesn't pay for an extra layer in this epic
A failed history fetch (network, 401, 404) shows the api() error message inline in the panel, and the next open retries
